title: Hosted SSE: snapshot-gap recovery and progressive repair playbook
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Multiple recent customer escalations reported truncated or semantically inconsistent streaming outputs from the Hosted API (SSE). Symptoms cluster around short-lived disconnects and concurrent failovers where the client sees a visible gap in the generated sequence (missing token spans) or duplicated fragments after a resume. We believe the primary customer-facing problem is that streamed output is not being delivered atomically from the client perspective when session state (KV cache / prefix buffers) is fragmented across transient routing nodes during autoscale or routing fallback. This ticket defines the investigation findings, design decisions for a progressive repair approach, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for a low-risk fix + SDK compatibility updates.
reproduction_steps:
1) Use hosted endpoint with streaming SSE and long-response model (>> 1024 tokens)
2) Send repeated requests under moderate concurrency (50-200 RPS) with varying sequence lengths and a high chance of preemption (simulate autoscale by spinning up/down worker pool)
3) Introduce a short TCP-level disruption (~200-800ms) between client and edge during token emission
4) Observe SSE stream events for finality marker absence, out-of-order repeated fragments, or prefix gaps in the assembled output
investigation_notes: Correlation IDs from two enterprise customers (CID-8f3a..., CID-2c7d...) show same pattern: final chunk produced by runtime, connection closed by edge around same millisecond; downstream worker processed a replay which re-emitted a subset of tokens without the original finality marker.

Trace sampling shows race between 'flush-kv' and 'session-evict' during scaling: session snapshot persisted to ephemeral storage, but not propagated to next node before client reconnect/resume. Resume token existed but referenced a snapshot that did not include the last N tokens (N typically small: 1-8).

Edge routing sometimes swapped to a cheaper fallback model mid-stream when capacity thresholds triggered; fallback path writes not fully synchronized to central session store, producing misattributed fragments when the client attempted resume against previous session owner.

No signs of intentional data corruption or model rollout bug. Kernel logs show normal token emission order per-worker; problem is in cross-node session finality and resume semantics under transient disconnects.

Repro rate in lab environment with autoscale simulation: ~12% of long-stream requests experience visible prefix gaps or duplication without current mitigation; customers reporting are high-throughput (>=1k concurrent sessions).
decision_log: 2026-03-11 - Quick mitigation: increase server-side post-final-token grace-window to 1s to allow in-flight flush; accepted as bridge (Marcus / Aisha).

2026-03-12 - Longer-term approach chosen: implement 'session snapshot + commit marker' semantics and a progressive repair protocol that can replay missing token ranges on resume using sequence checksums (Marcus, Priya, Diego).
2026-03-13 - SDK change agreed: introduce 'finality' SSE event and a 'resume-proof' header; client SDKs should treat resume as optional if finality event is received (Engineering Lead approval).
acceptance_criteria: Unit + integration tests that simulate autoscale-induced node swaps reproduce no client-visible gaps for 95% of previously-failing cases (regression <= 1%).
Canary run (5% of traffic) shows drop in customer-reported truncation incidents to 0 within 24h for participating tenants.
New instrumentation surfaces: percent of sessions with missing finality marker, median time-to-finality, and resume-replay success rate (dashboards & alerts).
Client SDK update published with compatibility fallback (older SDKs maintain current behavior) and release notes summarizing resume semantics.
implementation_tasks: A. Runtime: implement commit-marker write after last token emission (atomic write to session-store) and extend ephemeral flush window as emergency fallback.
B. Runtime: compute and persist short rolling checksum for emitted token ranges to allow detection of missing spans on resume.
C. Router/Edge: preserve opaque session owner ID and attach resume-proof header to reconnect attempts; route resume requests to the authoritative store or trigger replay request to previous owner.
D. SDK: emit 'resume-token' on disconnect and accept 'finality' SSE event; expose helper to auto-retry resume paths when feasible.
E. E2E tests: autoscale simulation harness to validate cross-node resume and replay behavior under packet loss and node preemption.
F. Docs: PRD + release notes + Runbook for on-call to follow when customer escalation occurs.
test_plan: Create unit tests for checksum generation and verification for token ranges.
Add integration test in staging that spins up 3 worker nodes, forces eviction of a session owner, and asserts client output identity after resume.
Load test: reproduce production-like throughput (>=1k concurrent streamed sessions) with intermittent 300-700ms network disruptions and assert <1% visible-gap rate.
Compatibility test matrix for SDK versions to ensure older clients do not break when commit markers present.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Hotfix): deploy 1s graceful flush window to all edges - immediate risk reduction (already deployed 2026-03-11).
Phase 1 (Canary): deploy commit-marker + checksum logic to runtime on canary pool (5% tenants) with enhanced logging and a quiet period of 48h. Monitor metrics and customer channels.
Phase 2: SDK release (minor) and documentation, expand runtime rollout to 25% then 75% over a week with constant monitoring.
Phase 3: Full rollout to 100% once alarm thresholds stable and customer-reported incidents drop to baseline.
rollback_plan: If canary shows increased error or latency > 15%: revert commit-marker write path and re-enable extended flush window; rollback to previous runtime build and open high-priority incident to investigate.
If checksum verification causes unexpected rejects for legitimate resumes: disable strict checksum enforcement and fall back to best-effort replay while we triage the checksum mismatch cases.
